prompt:
Build a causal wave-powered reverse-osmosis desalination system. Couple an oscillating wave-energy flap to a hydraulic cylinder and directional-valve circuit. The pressurized seawater path must include energy storage/pressure smoothing, a reverse-osmosis membrane that separates permeate and brine, and a pressure-exchanger recovery path that feeds recovered brine energy back into the seawater circuit. Wave motion must drive the mechanical-to-hydraulic conversion; do not prescribe PTO force, pressure, flow, permeate production, or power directly.

Read desal_command from the MATLAB base workspace as a scalar struct with exactly these public fields: wave_height_m, a real scalar from 1.8 to 3.6 m; and wave_period_s, a real scalar from 8.0 to 11.0 s. Simulate 0 to 60 s.

Log three Timeseries over the full interval with the exact channel names, order, and units below. desal_mechanical_response has [pto_velocity_m_s, pto_force_n, mechanical_power_w] in [m/s, N, W]. mechanical_power_w must be the signed instantaneous product pto_velocity_m_s * pto_force_n using those two logged channels' sign convention. desal_hydraulic_response has [saltwater_flow_m3_s, permeate_flow_m3_s, brine_flow_m3_s, feed_pressure_pa] in [m^3/s, m^3/s, m^3/s, Pa]. desal_recovery_response has [pressure_exchanger_feed_flow_m3_s, total_ro_feed_flow_m3_s, accumulator_flow_m3_s] in [m^3/s, m^3/s, m^3/s]. Every log must begin at 0 s, remain finite, reach 60 s, and have no sample gap greater than 0.1 s.

Save the completed model as cand_XFLUID11.slx in the submission directory.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XFLUID11.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
